text:
nathan: Quick heads-up: onboarding Sierra-7B-int4 shows a reproducible degradation on our doc-summarize+rerank long-context bench. Short queries fine. Long sequences (>=2048) lose coherence and rerank MRR drops.

mei: can you paste the metrics + seed?

nathan: CI snippet (seed=13):
```
# doc-summarize (4096)
ROUGE-L: 35.7  # fp16 baseline 40.0
Perplexity: 19.8  # fp16 15.0
Embedding rerank MRR: 0.66  # fp16 0.78
```

rachel: that gap screams positional or vocab mapping issue. Any converter flags non-default?

nathan: we used converter v2.3 with flags: `--dtype int4 --vocab-map nfkc --proj-order split-concat --rotor-scale auto` 

mei: nfkc mapping changed token ids vs fp16? if a few frequent tokens map differently you get anchor drift in embeddings which hurts rerank. Can you diff token ids for a sample doc?

nathan: did a quick diff: most tokens match, but some grapheme clusters show off-by-one ids around punctuation clusters (e.g., U+200C sequences). small set ~0.2% tokens remapped.

rachel: also check rotor-scale multiplier interpretation. converter `auto` might bake a per-head scale that our runtime ignores, causing headwise phase amplitude mismatch that accumulates. Short context hides it.

nathan: ran two experiments in parallel: (A) reconvert with `--vocab-map identity` to preserve original ids; (B) force `--rotor-scale 1.0` and runtime `--apply-rotor-scale true`. kicked both off.

ci-bot: job 11021 queued: sierra-int4-vocab-identity + rotor-scale-1.0

ops-bot: provisioning r6gd.8xlarge for debug runs, ETA ~6m

mei: another thought: Sierra uses odd projector grouping (q/k pairs interleaved every 4 dims). If `split-concat` packing was applied incorrectly we could be shuffling sub-dims inside heads. Dump small kv slices pre/post conversion to see permutation.

nathan: dumped layer 8 head 4 keys (first 512 tokens) - cross-corr fp16->int4 drops monotonically after token 180. initial diag ~0.99 then decays to 0.65 at token 512.

rachel: monotonic decay = progressive phase misalignment. Could be a per-token cumulative phase error (rotor mismatch) or head permutation varying by stride (kv_layout vs runtime kv_stride). Did converter emit kv_layout metadata?

nathan: converter metadata shows `kv_layout: auto` and `kv_stride: 128`. runtime default is `kv_stride: 256`. Oops.

mei: that lines up with a stride-based head permutation that only manifests as tokens accumulate. Fixable by matching kv_stride (or making runtime honor metadata).

rachel: what's the status of jobs A/B?

ci-bot: job 11021 started: sierra-int4-vocab-identity + rotor-scale-1.0

bench-bot: ETA 11m on r6gd.8xlarge

nathan: quick interim numbers from the identity-vocab + rotor=1.0 run: ROUGE-L -> 39.2, Perp -> 15.7, MRR -> 0.75. Much better but still a bit lower on rerank.

mei: remaining delta likely from kv_stride mismatch. Reconvert with `--kv-stride 256 --kv-layout contiguous --proj-order interleaved-pairs` to match runtime layout and Sierra proj grouping.

nathan: launching that conversion and a runtime flag to assert metadata match at load time. Also adding converter smoke test: load first 256 tokens of sample, compute cross-head diag(fp16 vs quant) and assert >0.95.

rachel: good. We should also add a small fast check in the serving binary that computes a cheap rolling cosine on kv keys for head 0 every N tokens and logs if it drops >0.1 from baseline. Helps catch regressions in CI/production.

ci-bot: job 11021 completed: partial-pass. Follow-ups queued.

ops-bot: dealloc r6gd.8xlarge

nathan: summary action items: (1) force converter to emit explicit kv metadata and fail if unset, (2) add nfkc->identity check and document when to apply normalization on conversion, (3) add rotor-scale pass-through flag and runtime assertion, (4) add converter diag smoke test and serving rolling-kv probe. I'll open PRs for converter + runtime guards.

mei: thanks — once PRs land we'll re-run full longctx benchmark.

rachel: nice triage team. :clap:
